field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The wind stayed down until noon and the anglers fished up the coast for rock fish, lingcod, and halibut. The fish were on the bite in the morning in 60-80 feet of water. The few anglers in the deep water caught a mix of bigger rock fish. There were some nice rock fish and a few halibut caught in front of the harbor. I did not hear of any tuna reports this weekend due to the wind.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast September 17, 2026 Big Albacore Highlight Eureka’s Weekend Tuna Run Gabe Gibbs of Montana made his first trip on the ocean a success by landing his first-ever Albacore. Gibbs is a current CR student and baseball player who was fishing on Steller Sunrise with Capt. Lowell Wallace Sunday. Photo courtesy of John Lanz It was a Saturday that Eureka tuna anglers won’t soon forget. After several less-than-stellar days, the stars finally aligned for the small fleet that made the 30- to 35-mile run south. It wasn’t the number of fish that stood out — it was the size. The majority of the albacore caught were 25 pounds or better, with some fish pushing 40 pounds. The fish were reportedly spread out along the 125-line, from the 46-line down to the 38-line, where a hard break pushed water temperatures up six degrees. The action ranged from boats reporting single hookups to others hooking eight at a time, and everything in between. A couple of common themes emerged from the fleet: when the fish are this big, you only have room for so many, and several anglers left fish biting at the end of the day. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: Good day for the Dockside bottom fishing boats limiting almost everyone on six boats out this morning. Quite a few Lingcod were caught as the Lingcod bite is improving it seems by the day and crabbing has been good on most boats for the past few days.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: Today was the best day of the year. SNB was plugged by noon. Legendz is on a 2 hour, 80 fish stop. Pretty much every sport boat was plugged today. The wind is blowing tomorrow, but we will be out there on Monday. ​Mike C 9/17 & 9/18. Slow then great fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) in consultation with the State of Oregon, the Pacific Fishery Management Council, and fishery representatives met today via conference call and have taken the following in-season management action related to the ocean recreational non-mark-selective coho salmon season from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain: ACTIONS TAKEN: • Effective Sunday, September 20, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 20, 2026 at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement).
